merge_algorithm_note: An initial attempt used transitive (union-find) merging, which produced pathological chaining -- e.g. 13 of 18 positive clusters collapsed into one group at a similarity threshold of 0.58, because union-find merges A with C whenever A-B and B-C both cross the threshold, regardless of A-C similarity. Average-linkage agglomerative clustering (scipy.cluster.hierarchy, method='average') was used instead, which requires the AVERAGE similarity across an entire candidate group to clear the threshold, not just one connecting pair. This resisted chaining and produced the modest, semantically coherent consolidation reflected in this file (18->11 positive, 20->15 negative).
key_finding: The 'Forced Copilot integration' theme (135 phrases, 1.9% of negative pairs) was NOT merged with any other cluster despite the consolidation step -- visible in merge_dendrograms.png as the cluster branching off at the highest distance in the negative dendrogram (cluster 16, leftmost leaf). This independently corroborates, from real app-review text, the qualitative web-search pass's finding that a meaningful share of Windows Copilot dissatisfaction concerns unwanted, forced OS-level integration rather than output quality -- part of a three-method triangulation argument in the paper's Discussion section.
